meta.title: A New Game for Saturday
meta.textType: dialogue: where and when to meet

paragraphs: On Friday, Sam went to the school shop to buy a magazine about sports. May saw him at the door and asked, "What is in your magazine?" "There are games from many countries," said Sam. "Look at this game. It has two teams, one ball, and three boxes." May read the page and was surprised. "The game has no winner," she said. "Everybody plays together." "Let's invent our own game," said Sam. "When shall we play it?" asked May.

"Can we play on Saturday?" asked Sam. "Pat and I go to the library with Mom until half past ten," said May. "Then we can meet at eleven o'clock." "Eleven is good for me," said Sam. "Where shall we meet?" "Let's meet under the big tree next to the pond," said May. "It is a good place for a game." "Shall I ask Lily and Mia?" asked Sam. "Yes, please," said May.

At lunch, Sam found Lily and Mia in the canteen. He told them the plan. "We need three boxes," said Lily. "Dad has some boxes at home. I can bring them." "I have a soft ball," said Mia. Sam wrote a note on a piece of paper. It said, "Saturday, eleven o'clock, under the big tree next to the pond." Each child read the note and said, "OK!"

On Saturday, the children came to the pond at eleven o'clock. Pat was surprised to see three big boxes under the tree. They made two teams, and Pip sat in one box. The children threw the ball into the boxes and laughed. "Who is the winner?" asked Pat. "Everybody is a winner," said May. It was a very good game.
text.summary: Sam and May read about a game in a magazine and decide to invent their own. They choose the place and the time and ask Lily and Mia to come.
